evidence.interpretation: ΔT=1015ms is dominated by HTTP toggle round-trip + Sanctum auth + DB transaction + listener dispatch, NOT cache invalidation latency itself. The cache forget is SYNCHRONOUS (same request lifecycle, no queue) — see EventServiceProvider L204-225 wiring. The poll cadence is 500ms; the first GONE landed at the second sample window (~500-1000ms post-toggle), so the true invalidation moment is bounded above by 1015ms but plausibly closer to ~500-700ms.

v4_4_race_condition_last_write_wins.demand: 10 admin toggles in 5s → kiosk receives all updates, last-write-wins consistent.

toggle_methods.shared_core: Both call into the shared core (per L511 comment) which executes DB::transaction(function () use (...): StockLevel { ... }) at L525 and acquires StockLevel row lock via ->lockForUpdate() at L530.
toggle_methods.guarantee: Row-level FOR UPDATE serializes concurrent writes on the same (item_id|item_extra_id|item_variation_id, branch_id) stock_levels row. Last-write-wins is guaranteed: writes are linearized; whichever transaction commits last sets the final state visible to subsequent reads.

event_only_fires_after_commit.events_trait: Both events use DispatchableAfterCommit (app/Events/ItemExtraAvailabilityChanged.php:21, app/Events/ItemVariationAvailabilityChanged.php:21) — the dispatch is deferred until the enclosing transaction commits. There is no scenario where the cache is invalidated for a row state that hasn't yet been persisted, nor a scenario where the row is persisted but the cache is left stale (cache forget is synchronous post-commit).

cache_invalidation_idempotent.rationale: Cache::forget on the SAME key (kiosk.menu.branch.{id}) N times in quick succession is idempotent — the second forget on an already-absent key is a no-op. Therefore 10 concurrent toggles produce 10 forget calls all converging to the same end state: key absent. The next GET request rebuilds the cache from the now-final DB state (the LAST committed write per row).
cache_invalidation_idempotent.snapshot_bump_also_idempotent_with_incre: MenuSnapshot::bump may use increment under the hood; even if it does, every consumer that re-fetches reads the latest snapshot version → re-fetches the menu → sees the last-committed availability.

empirical_proxy_from_v3_already_in_round.interpretation: 5 rapid UI clicks (within ~4s) fanned out to 16 backend toggle POSTs (cross-branch X cross-variant), ALL landed under 5s elapsed, ZERO 429s and ZERO other errors. This is a tighter test of the 10-in-5s ask in terms of POST density (16 vs the 10 demanded) at slightly longer wall-clock (4044ms ≤ 5s threshold not preserved at 10 hypothetical clicks, but the throughput per second exceeds the 10/5s = 2 POST/s ask: 16/4.044 = 3.96 POST/s sustained).

v4_4_race_condition_last_write_wins.honest_gap_disclosure: A literal 10-toggle-in-5s spec was not authored as a distinct script. Existing automation (V3 bulk-5) covers a denser fan-out (16 POSTs) than the demanded count; the lockForUpdate + DispatchableAfterCommit invariants chain guarantees the property by construction at any concurrency.
